messages.content: i went to a small restaurant after school with my father. we usually sit near the door, but today we sat by the window. it made the place feel new even though we had been there before.
a small change in where you sit can change what you see. what did you see from the window that you had not seen from the door?
i could see people waiting at the station across the road. my father said he used to wait there when he was young.
then the new place to sit gave you something else to talk about together. did he tell you about the journey he used to take?
he said he took the train to school. i had never asked him about that before. i knew where he studied, but not how he got there.
that is a nice detail to learn from a simple meal together. knowing the place he went to school was one part. hearing about the journey gave you another part of his day.
i want to ask more, but not make him tell his whole life at once.
you could ask one question about the journey. for example: what did you like to do while you waited for the train?
he said he usually read. i do that when i wait too.
you read while waiting now, and your father read while waiting when he was young. you can tell him what you read and ask what kind of book he carried then.
make that simple.
you both enjoy reading while waiting. you can share what you read now and ask about his books from before.
say that with the difference in time clear.
you read while waiting now, and your father read while waiting when he was young.
a teacher told me she would leave two books for me at the front desk. when i got there, i saw three books. does that mean all three are for me?
not from the number alone. the teacher said two books were for you. you can ask which two before taking all the books you see.
there is a note on one book with my name. the other two have no note.
then you have a clear detail about one book, but not enough to choose the other one. ask the teacher or the person at the desk which other book was left for you.
say that in two short sentences.
one book has your name. you still need to ask which other book is for you.
can i take the one with my name while i ask about the rest?
you can ask the person at the desk whether it is ready for you to take. the note helps make the book clear, but you can still check what to do next.
write that question for the person at the desk.
is this book with my name for me to take, and do you know which other book the teacher left for me?
they say only the one with my name is ready. the other will come tomorrow.
then the plan is to take the ready book now and get the other one tomorrow, if that is what they told you to do. the two other books on the desk were not made yours by being near it.
write a short message to the teacher saying what happened.
i found one book with my name and was told the other will be ready tomorrow. thank you for leaving them for me.
write a story about a girl walking through town with her grandfather. he can remember how one place looked before, but she likes it as it is now. neither has to make the other change their mind.

a girl and her grandfather walked through town after lunch. near the library, he stopped and said there had once been a garden in that place. he remembered sitting under a tree while waiting for a friend. the girl looked at the library window and said she liked going there to read. her grandfather said he liked that too, although he still remembered the garden. they stood for a moment, looking at the same place with different pictures in mind. then the girl asked if he wanted to come inside with her. he said yes, and they went to look for a book.
can you make the first part clear without saying the garden and library were there at the same time?
you can say: the garden had been there before the library was built. her grandfather remembered the garden, while the girl knew the place as a library.
what does although do in your story?
it keeps both parts together: he likes the library, and he still can remember the garden. he can enjoy what is there now without the old memory going away.
write their conversation in a few short sentences.
there used to be a garden here. i liked sitting under its tree. i like the library here now. i do too, but i still remember the garden. would you like to go inside? yes, let us find a book.
what if i want a sad story instead?
you could let him feel sad about the lost garden without saying the girl is wrong because she likes the library. the same place can bring different feelings to both people.
keep it as it is. give me a short last line.
together, they went inside to find something new to read.
i have a free afternoon and many things i could do. i keep changing my mind, so i have not started anything.
would you rather use the afternoon to finish one task, enjoy something, or rest? choosing the kind of time you want may help before choosing a specific thing.
i want to enjoy something. i have already done enough work today.
then you can leave the work list alone for now. what is one thing you usually enjoy that is easy to begin?
i like drawing, but i always think i need a whole idea before i start.
you could start with something in front of you, such as a cup near your hand. the first drawing does not have to become a large finished picture.
keep the cup example simple.
you could draw a cup that is already near you. you do not need to choose a whole story for the picture before you begin.
can you give me one question to ask myself while i draw?
what do i see in the shape of this cup when i look at it slowly?
that sounds like work too. i just want to make something, even if it is not like a real cup.
then you can let the cup be a starting idea rather than a thing that must look the same in your picture. you could make it a different color, a different size, or part of a made up place.
make the last reply simple.
you can start with the cup and change it in your drawing. it does not have to look like the real one for you to enjoy making the picture.
my mother asked my brother to bring bread. i heard her say it while i was leaving. now i am at the shop. does hearing it make the task mine?
no. the request was for your brother. you can choose to help, but hearing the words does not by itself change who was asked.
i could buy it and tell him, but i do not want us both to buy bread.
then check with him before buying it if you can. you could say you are at the shop and ask whether he has already got the bread.
write that message.
i am at the shop. have you already bought the bread, or would you like me to get it?
he says he has not bought it and asks me to get it. what changed?
now he has asked you to do that part, and you can answer whether you will. the task did not become yours just from hearing your mother. it changed through this conversation.
i say yes. now write a message i can send my mother, keeping the people clear.
i asked my brother about the bread. he had not bought it, so i said i would get it while i am at the shop.
why say had not bought instead of has not bought?
had not bought looks back to when you asked him. has not bought is about what is true now. in your message, you are telling the order of the conversation and your choice after his answer.
can i leave that explanation out of the message?
yes. the message only needs the plan. you can say: i am getting the bread from the shop, so my brother does not need to buy it too.
i want to send a voice message to my cousin, but i keep starting over because i do not like my words. i am only telling her about my day.
you do not need a long explanation to tell a cousin about your day. you could choose one or two things you want to share and talk as you would in a simple conversation.
say it with message.
your message can be simple. choose one or two things from your day and talk about those.
i went for a walk and saw a friend at the park. we sat together for a while. that is what i want to say.
you could start: i went for a walk today and saw a friend at the park. we sat together for a little while.
we sat quietly. i liked that, and i want to add it.
i went for a walk today and saw a friend at the park. we sat quietly together for a while, and i liked having that time.
ask me one question that might help me say more.
what did you like about sitting quietly with your friend?
i did not have to find something to say. i could just look at the trees and know someone was there with me.
that is a clear thing to share. you can add: i liked not having to keep talking. we could just sit near the trees together.
make it one short message with the walk too.
i went for a walk and saw a friend at the park. we sat quietly near the trees, and i liked being together without having to keep talking.
is if my sister comes, i will make tea the same as when my sister comes, i will make tea?
they are similar, but if can leave open whether she will come. when can speak as though she is coming and say what you will do then. the rest of the conversation helps make the meaning clear.
keep it simple.
if can leave open whether she will come. when can speak as though she is coming and say what you will do then. the rest of the conversation helps make the meaning clear.
so if does not mean she will not come?
right. it does not choose no. it leaves her coming open and says you will make tea if she does come.
use simple words again.
if does not mean she will not come. it leaves that part open and says you will make tea if she does.
now she has told me she will come at four. which sentence would be clear?
you could say: when my sister comes at four, i will make tea. that works with the plan you now have.
what if i only want tea if she wants some too?
then say: when my sister comes at four, i will ask whether she wants tea. if she does, i will make some.
does that make the difference between the visit and the tea choice clear?
yes. the visit will be at four. making tea is still something you will choose after asking what she wants.
picoboi, do not answer this question yet. just make it shorter: would you please tell me whether there is any way we could meet at a time after lunch tomorrow?
could we meet after lunch tomorrow?
now explain what you did.
i kept the question about meeting after lunch tomorrow and left out words that made it longer. i did not choose yes or no for the other person.
explain simply.
i kept the time and the request to meet. i made the question shorter without answering it.
now write a possible yes from a friend, but say it is made up.
a made up answer could be: yes, after lunch tomorrow works for me.
does your example mean my real friend said yes?
no. that answer was an example you asked me to make up. your real friend has not answered in the information you gave me.
ask my last question in a simple way.
does your example mean my real friend said yes?
now answer that question with one short sentence.
no, the example is made up and is not an answer from your real friend.
